scenes.narration: [serious] Police hacked a gang of hackers and took over their website.
The gang was called LockBit. They locked files and asked for money to unlock them. Over 2,500 victims.
Then, on February 19, 2024, police struck back. They shut down 34 of the gang's computers.
The gang's own website now showed police messages. Police also took 1,000 keys to unlock files.
Then a countdown appeared on the site. It asked, who is LockBitSupp? That was the gang's boss.
In May 2024, America named him: Dmitry Khoroshev, officials say. There is a 10 million dollar reward.
He is probably still in Russia. But everyone knows his name now.

facts.claim: On February 19, 2024 the UK National Crime Agency led Operation Cronos, seized LockBit's leak site, took down 34 servers in eight countries and obtained over 1,000 decryption keys
The seized leak site displayed law-enforcement content; one page asked 'Who is LockbitSupp?' with a countdown clock
The DOJ says LockBit attacked more than 2,500 victims in at least 120 countries
In May 2024 the U.S. charged Russian national Dmitry Khoroshev in a 26-count indictment, alleging he is LockBitSupp; a $10 million reward is offered
Khoroshev lives in Russia, so extradition is considered unlikely

seo.title: LockBit Takedown: How Police Hacked a Ransomware Gang
seo.description: In February 2024, Britain's National Crime Agency took over LockBit's own leak site in Operation Cronos. Months later, U.S. prosecutors charged the man they say ran it. Learn how the LockBit ransomware takedown (Operation Cronos) worked. #cybersecurity #lockbit #ransomware #shorts
